text_blocks.snippet: The International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) is a questionnaire used to assess the severity of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in men, primarily those related to benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). It involves answering eight questions about urinary symptoms and quality of life, with scores ranging from 0 to 35.
snippet_highlighted_words: a questionnaire used to assess the severity of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in men, primarily those related to benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a breakdown of the IPSS:

list.title: Purpose:
list.snippet: To evaluate the severity of urinary symptoms (like incomplete emptying, frequency, intermittency, urgency, weak stream, straining, and nocturia) and quality of life related to these symptoms.

list.title: Structure:
list.snippet: The IPSS questionnaire consists of eight questions. The first seven address urinary symptoms experienced in the past month, with each question having six possible answers, scored from 0 to 5.
Each of the seven symptom questions is scored from 0 (not at all) to 5 (almost always).
